newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa to leave hospital on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa to leave hospital on Thursday.

text.p: Mother Teresa will be released from hospital on Thursday, three weeks after undergoing heart surgery, and return to her religious order, an official at an Indian heart clinic said.

"She is leaving today. We are discharging her. She is all right," S.K. Tiwari, administrator of Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre, told Reuters. Last month the 86-year-old nun had her third heart operation in five years.

The revered Roman Catholic missionary, fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, was taken to hospital on November 22 after suffering heart failure. It was the third time since August that she had been admitted to hospital for emergency care.
Doctors operated on her on November 29, unblocking two coronary arteries with a tiny balloon. The surgery, during which she was under general anaesthesia, was successful.
But a faltering heartbeat and long-standing lung and kidney problems delayed her recovery. Twice in the past week doctors have given her a mild electric shock to correct her heartbeat.
On Wednesday doctors said nagging bronchitis, which has periodically dogged Mother Teresa from her youth, had finally cleared up.
The 1979 Nobel peace prize winner had been pressing doctors to let her return to her Missionaries of Charity religious order, playfully asking nuns to order an ambulance to take her home.
Mother Teresa was born Agnes Goinxha Bejaxhiu to Albanian parents in Skopje, in what was then Serbia, on August 27, 1910.
Known as the "Saint of the Gutters", Mother Teresa has become an international byword for devotion to the poor, destitute and dying during nearly 50 years of work.
She began her missionary work in 1948 in Calcutta, India's most densely populated city.

Her Missionaries of Charity order has about 4,500 nuns operating in 111 countries. It feeds about 500,000 families each year, teaches 20,000 children in its schools and treats 90,000 lepers in its clinic.
